fixes.summary: Adopt one WorkCounters contract with two axes that are never summed: a PROVENANCE axis (jvp_calls/jvp_vectors = number of user JVP callback invocations/vectors actually executed, on every lane; explicit dense J*v products go to a new jacobian_matvecs counter) and a ROLE axis (linear_matvecs, recycle_refresh_matvecs, diagnostic_matvecs, block_matvecs = solver-level operator applications by purpose). Enforce it by making provenance a property of the operator instead of the call site: the JVP-backed ClosureOperator built in OdeProblem::linearize/linearize_matrix_free reports application_work {jvp_calls:1,jvp_vectors:1}, DenseOperator reports {jacobian_matvecs:1}, ShiftedOperator::new derives its work from the inner operator plus mass, and apply_jvp_counted charges jacobian.application_work() instead of an unconditional +1 (today it charges jvp_calls for dense matvecs: 140 with 0 callbacks). new_counted_jvp becomes a thin alias so the matrix-free lane keeps its exact E-08 values; bump a work_counters_semantics_version so frozen generic-lane ledgers are marked v1 and never compared with v2.
fixes.verification: Re-run the E-08 harness (harness/src/bin/e08_work_counters.rs) with the pre-registered rule replaced by `counters.jvp_calls == atomic.jvp` on all 24 arms: generic GMRES arm must read 760 (PR) and 74897 (robertson n=96) instead of 140/8841, PR-with-jac must read jvp_calls=0 and jacobian_matvecs=760, and the 12 matrix-free arms must stay at difference 0. rhs_calls/ft_calls and all solution bits must be unchanged (accounting-only change).

fixes.summary: Add one integrator-level contract test that runs the SAME JVP-only problem through both lanes (generic integrate_adaptive_observed_with_config + LinearMethod::Gmres, and the strict matrix-free lane built on build_step_context_matrix_free) with the JVP closure wrapped in an AtomicU64, and asserts jvp_calls == jvp_vectors == atomic count on each lane, including an arm with forced GMRES failures and step rejections. A third arm with an explicit Jacobian asserts jvp_calls == 0 and jacobian_matvecs > 0. The existing operator_accounting_contracts.rs:36 assertion only covers the block path and would not fail on today's generic-lane undercount.
fixes.verification: The new test must FAIL on b3e8165 (generic lane 140 != 760) and PASS after the operator-provenance fix; keep it in the default `cargo test -p rodas5p-integrators` set so any future call site that bypasses apply_counted/apply_jvp_counted breaks it.

fixes.summary: Parse and derive the RODAS5P tableau once per process in a std::sync::OnceLock and hand out &'static Rodas5pCoefficients; load_rodas5p_coefficients() stays as a cloning compatibility wrapper for tests and the CLI. StepContext.coeffs becomes &'static Rodas5pCoefficients (field reads keep compiling through auto-deref) and sequential.rs:154/:202, dense_output_v2.rs:82 and stage_batch.rs:173 (plus homotopy.rs, common_w_gate.rs) switch to the cached accessor. Expected effect: removes one serde_json parse of 4430 bytes, about 110 decimal parses, an 8x8 inverse and three matmuls from every step attempt and every interior dense-output sample (the audit's unmeasured estimate is 10-40 us each); results are bit-identical because the derivation is deterministic, only wall time changes, and the additive constant that compresses candidate/baseline ratios toward 1 on small-n corpora disappears.
fixes.verification: (1) Unit test: rodas5p_coefficients() returns the same pointer twice and equals a fresh parse field-by-field with to_bits(). (2) Scientific checksums of the fair-ab fixed and adaptive screens unchanged before/after. (3) Build exp/D6/coeff_bench.rs against the patched crates and record per-call cost before (full load) and after (pointer read); re-time E-08 robertson n=96 mf_adaptive_reject under the new timing protocol to report the measured share instead of the estimate.

fixes.summary: Counting rule for Block GMRES: linear_matvecs and preconditioner_apps remain SOLVER-LEVEL application counts (one apply of the s*n operator = 1), and two vector-unit counters are added, linear_matvec_vectors and preconditioner_vectors, charged in n-vector equivalents (s=8 per block apply, 1 per sequential apply). The unit comes from the object, not the caller: OperatorApplicationWork gains state_vectors (BlockOperator returns s, ShiftedOperator returns 1) and Preconditioner gains application_vectors() (BlockDirectPc and BlockJacobiPc return s); apply_counted/apply_preconditioner charge them. BlockSolveReport gains matvec_vectors/preconditioner_vectors, any block-vs-sequential comparison must read only the *_vectors fields, and unified_screen batch_vectors = 8*block_linear_solves is replaced by the counted value.
fixes.verification: Extend block_gmres_charges_every_stage_jvp_and_mass_action_at_the_operator_site with BlockPreconditioner::Direct: assert delta.linear_matvec_vectors == s*(linear_matvecs+diagnostic_matvecs) == delta.jvp_vectors and delta.preconditioner_vectors == s*delta.preconditioner_apps; add a sequential-GMRES twin asserting linear_matvec_vectors == linear_matvecs. Assert unified_screen batch_vectors equals the counted preconditioner/solve vectors on one SABR block solve.

fixes.summary: Counting rule for failed trials: every attempt (accepted, rejected by the embedded estimate, or aborted by NonFinite/LinearSolve) charges all of its WorkCounters to the trajectory total and nothing is ever rolled back, which is the behaviour E-08 already observed on the production lanes. In g4_s5b0_regime_atlas::run_trajectory, merge the whole step_counters into a trajectory total immediately after the trial returns (before any `continue`), emit the totals plus an accepted/rejected/failed split in G4S5B0TrajectorySummary, and keep per-accepted-step rows as they are. Until regenerated, mark outputs of this runner `legacy-accepted-only-work` so its R-JF cost figures are not compared with the v3.x attempt-row runners. Same rule for error returns: a path that returns Err must leave the caller's counters charged (E-08 notes the fixed direct path drops them).
anchors: exp/E-08/README.md (forced failures counted, never rolled back)
fixes.verification: New test: run the atlas trajectory on a profile with h0 forced large enough to reject at least once, with rhs/jvp closures wrapped in AtomicU64; assert summary.total_rhs_evaluations == atomic rhs, summary.total_jvp_vectors == atomic jvp, rejected_steps > 0, and total > sum of accepted rows. Must fail on b3e8165 where rejected/failed work is absent from the summary.

fixes.summary: Two-tier comparator policy. Tier A (minimum fairness, required before any RODAS5P-vs-comparator front on RhsCalls, DirectFactorizations or WallSeconds may be read as performance): Newton stopping tolerance scaled by the outer tolerance (SciPy Radau rule kappa = max(10*eps/rtol, min(0.03, sqrt(rtol))), CVODE-style 0.1 for BDF) measured in the same atol/rtol WRMS norm, and Jacobian/LU reuse across Newton iterations and across steps with refactorization only on h*gamma change beyond a threshold or on slow convergence, so direct_factorizations reflects a modified-Newton implementation. Tier B (what ships today): every record, front and attainment produced with NewtonConfig::default() or RadauConfig::default() carries comparator_fidelity = "reference-implementation-only" and mixed fronts carry comparative_reading = "forbidden"; the fair-ab writer and the G3/unified gates refuse to emit a relative-performance verdict against a Tier-B comparator. This turns the README.md:27 disclosure into a machine-checked field.
fixes.verification: Tier B (XS, ship first): schema test that every comparator row serializes comparator_fidelity and that a gate given a reference-only comparator returns NotEvaluated instead of Promote/Block. Tier A: (1) Radau IIA3 and BDF2 on Prothero-Robinson and robertson at rtol 1e-4 vs 1e-8 must show Newton iterations per step decreasing with looser rtol while global error stays within the fair-ab tolerance band; (2) direct_factorizations per accepted step < 1 on a constant-h linear problem; (3) frozen scientific checksums of the existing Tier-B runs unchanged because the default configs are kept under the reference-only label.

fixes.summary: The RadauIIA3 error estimate factorizes (mu/h)M - J on every trial in addition to the 3n stage system; that matrix is exactly SciPy's LU_real, which a faithful Radau already owns. Minimal fix: cache the estimator LU in the step kernel keyed on (h bits, frozen-Jacobian token) so rejections with unchanged h/J and the previous_local_rejection re-solve reuse it, and charge it to a separate estimator_factorizations counter so direct_factorizations-based comparisons can exclude or include it explicitly. Full fix (part of Tier A above): replace the dense 3n real Newton system by the standard real/complex split, one n x n real LU shared with the estimate plus one n x n complex LU, roughly 5 n^3/3-equivalents instead of 27 n^3/3 + n^3/3 per factorization event. Until then frozen-radau-iia3 stays reference-implementation-only in the G3 and unified gates.
fixes.verification: Unit test on a linear constant-coefficient problem with a forced rejection followed by a retry at the same h: estimator_factorizations == 1 across both trials, error_norm bit-identical to the uncached path. For the split form: stage values and embedded error agree with the 3n formulation to 1e-12 relative on Prothero-Robinson and robertson, and direct_factorizations per accepted step drops accordingly.

fixes.summary: Replace `median ratio >= 1.15` by a paired timing protocol with a dispersion-aware decision. Per case: at least 2 warmups (batch size calibrated from the MINIMUM warmup sample, not the last), then at least 30 interleaved candidate/reference pairs in seeded random ABBA order on one pinned thread; the statistic is the median of per-pair log(reference/candidate), with a seeded case-clustered bootstrap (B=10000, percentile 95% CI) for the corpus-level speedup. Decision is three-valued: Promote iff CI lower bound >= 1.15, Block iff CI upper bound < 1.15, otherwise Inconclusive; an A/A control (reference vs reference) is run in the same session and the whole timing is declared non-authoritative if its CI excludes 1.0 or its half-width exceeds ln(1.15)/2. Smoke profiles (repetitions=1, warmups=0) and single-sample parallel timings may never emit Promote/Block on wall time, WallSeconds fronts are built only from authoritative reports, and each report records host metadata (CPU model, governor, load average, thread count, pinning).
fixes.verification: (1) Deterministic unit tests on synthetic samples: true ratio 1.30 with 5% noise -> Promote; true ratio 1.15 with the v3.6 recorded spread (pair ratios 0.547-4.43) -> Inconclusive; identical arms -> A/A CI contains 1.0; same seed -> identical CI bits. (2) Test that the Smoke profile yields NotEvaluated for the wall blocker. (3) Experiment: rerun the v3.6 N=384 paired-wall case under the new protocol after the OnceLock fix and record CI width; the gate is usable only if the A/A half-width is below ln(1.15)/2.
